citation: Komorowska, K., Doyle, A., Wahlestedt, M., et al. (2017). Hepatic Leukemia Factor Maintains Quiescence of Hematopoietic Stem Cells and Protects the Stem Cell Pool during Regeneration. Cell Reports 21, 3514–3523.
support: Mouse Hlf deletion impaired regenerative HSC maintenance and reduced quiescence. This supports Hlf-associated context, not quiescence measurements in Singh cells.

citation: Yokomizo, T., Watanabe, N., Umemoto, T., et al. (2019). Hlf marks the developmental pathway for hematopoietic stem cells but not for erythro-myeloid progenitors. Journal of Experimental Medicine 216, 1599–1614.
support: Developmental mouse Hlf-positive cells contained Hlf, Mecom and Procr-associated HSC expression; developmental setting, not an adult lineage identity classifier.

citation: Khanna, M., Wu, H., Johansson, C., Caizergues-Ferrer, M., and Feigon, J. (2006). Structural study of the H/ACA snoRNP components Nop10p and the 3-prime hairpin of U65 snoRNA. RNA 12, 40–52.
support: Nop10-related snoRNP structure and RNA modification. Molecular-function support, not hematopoietic-state evidence.

citation: Balsa, E., Marco, R., Perales-Clemente, E., Szklarczyk, R., Calvo, E., Landazuri, M.O., and Enriquez, J.A. (2012). NDUFA4 is a subunit of complex IV of the mammalian electron transport chain. Cell Metabolism 16, 378–386.
support: NDUFA4 respiratory-complex-IV function; does not measure metabolic flux here.

citation: Passegue, E., Wagers, A.J., Giuriato, S., Anderson, W.C., and Weissman, I.L. (2005). Global analysis of proliferation and cell cycle gene expression in the regulation of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell fates. Journal of Experimental Medicine 202, 1599–1611.
support: Primary HSPC cell-cycle and proliferation study; contextualizes phase-associated expression without equating NMF usage with division rate.

citation: van Galen, P., Mbong, N., Kreso, A., Schoof, E.M., Wagenblast, E., Ng, S.W.K., Krivdova, G., Jin, L., Nakauchi, H., and Dick, J.E. (2018). Integrated Stress Response Activity Marks Stem Cells in Normal Hematopoiesis and Leukemia. Cell Reports 25, 1109–1117.e5.
support: Primary human HSC study links ATF4/ISR and amino-acid deprivation response with persistence. Prevents interpreting stress-associated expression as loss of stem function.

citation: Laurenti, E., Frelin, C., Xie, S., et al. (2015). CDK6 levels regulate quiescence exit in human hematopoietic stem cells. Cell Stem Cell 16, 302–313.
support: CDK6 protein governs quiescence-exit kinetics in purified human HSC subsets. This motivates activation-associated interpretation, not proof from RNA or a new HSC subdivision.

citation: Boles, N.C., Lin, K.K., Lukov, G.L., Bowman, T.V., Baldridge, M.T., and Goodell, M.A. (2011). CD48 on hematopoietic progenitors regulates stem cells and suppresses tumor formation. Blood 118, 80–87.
support: CD48 protein was present on short-term progenitors and excluded from quiescent LT-HSCs in the examined mouse setting. Not a direct classification from Cd48 RNA here.

citation: Ng, S.S., De Labastida Rivera, F., Yan, J., et al. (2020). The NK cell granule protein NKG7 regulates cytotoxic granule exocytosis and inflammation. Nature Immunology 21, 1205–1218.
support: NKG7 granule/immune-effector function; its presence alongside heterogeneous genes does not establish NK identity.

citation: Wang, D., Zheng, M., Qiu, Y., et al. (2014). Tespa1 negatively regulates Fc-epsilon-RI-mediated signaling and the mast cell-mediated allergic response. Journal of Experimental Medicine.
support: Tespa1 participates in mast-cell receptor signaling, demonstrating that this P5 anchor is not a platelet-specific marker.

citation: Takubo, K., Nagamatsu, G., Kobayashi, C.I., et al. (2013). Regulation of glycolysis by Pdk functions as a metabolic checkpoint for cell cycle quiescence in hematopoietic stem cells. Cell Stem Cell 12, 49–61.
support: Functional mouse HSC evidence that glycolysis can support quiescence; forbids treating a glycolytic RNA program as a universal differentiation-speed marker.

citation: Ficara, F., Murphy, M.J., Lin, M., and Cleary, M.L. (2008). Pbx1 regulates self-renewal of long-term hematopoietic stem cells by maintaining their quiescence. Cell Stem Cell 2, 484–496.
support: Conditional mouse Pbx1 deletion altered HSC maintenance and TGF-beta responses; context for a loaded regulator, not proof of the corresponding function in MC3.

citation: Goossens, S., Janzen, V., Bartunkova, S., et al. (2011). The EMT regulator Zeb2/Sip1 is essential for murine embryonic hematopoietic stem/progenitor cell differentiation and mobilization. Blood.
support: Zeb2 deletion alters embryonic HSPC differentiation, mobilization and adhesion. Supports hematopoietic relevance rather than the misleading neuronal label; does not imply the same embryonic mechanism here.
